title: What If a Country Built a Capital From Nothing in 41 Months? Brazil Did

scenes.text: What if a country built a brand-new capital from empty grassland in under four years? Brazil did.
1956: President Kubitschek ordered a capital on the empty central plateau, about a thousand kilometres from Rio.
Lúcio Costa drew the city in the shape of a bird in flight. Oscar Niemeyer designed the buildings.
Around sixty thousand workers poured in from across Brazil. They dammed a river for a 48-square-kilometre lake.
Inaugurated April 21st, 1960, forty-one months after work began. Built for 500,000 people.
Today nearly three million live there, it's a UNESCO World Heritage site, and the bill was never fully counted.

description:
What if a country built a new capital from nothing? Brazil did: Brasília was built on the empty central plateau and inaugurated on 21 April 1960, about 41 months after construction began under President Juscelino Kubitschek.
Lúcio Costa's plan, often compared to a bird in flight, and Oscar Niemeyer's buildings were raised by around 60,000 workers; Lake Paranoá was dammed during construction. Planned for 500,000 people, the Federal District passed 2.8 million in the 2022 census. UNESCO listed it in 1987 as the first modern city on the World Heritage List. Its total cost was never reliably added up.
What should we run through next?
